note: Per-kind discipline: the premise shape, the falsifier, and the question the agentic pass asks. The ENGINE IS SHARED -- harness, suites, docker, ledger format are identical across kinds. Only the discipline differs, which is why this is a data file and not eleven forks.

tiers.proven: a discipline worked out against real instances in this system
tiers.designed: the falsifier question is stated; no instance built yet, so the pack ships the open question rather than a confident answer

forecaster.one_line: says what will happen, by when
forecaster.falsifier: the date arrives with the observable in another state
forecaster.predict_frame: Observe the entity and state what you EXPECT to see by the resolution date. Every claim needs an observable a stranger could check and a date. A claim with no date is not a forecast.
forecaster.assess_frame: The date has arrived. Did the stated observable reach the stated state? Grade hit / partial / miss / unresolvable, and say which.

decision-model.one_line: derives a person's decision function from their completed choices
decision-model.premise_shape: Given <recurring decision situation>, <actor> chooses <option A> over <option B>. Revealed by: <2+ completed, announced decisions>. Violated by: <a future choice that breaks the ordering>.
decision-model.falsifier: a future choice, in the named situation, that takes the other option
decision-model.predict_frame: Observe ONLY completed, announced decisions -- signed contracts, executed instructions, confirmed changes. Ignore rumour, 'reportedly considering', and statements of intent: the model's whole claim is that actions reveal what statements conceal. For each premise, report whether a decision since the model was written CONFORMS TO or VIOLATES the stated ordering, and say plainly if no qualifying decision has occurred.
decision-model.assess_frame: Did a completed decision in the named situation take the predicted option? A decision that never arose is UNRESOLVABLE, not a miss.
decision-model.banned: Psychology. 'X is loyal / ruthless / insecure' admits no future observation that settles it. Only orderings over choices.
decision-model.scope: Public figures acting in public roles, professional decisions only. Tag --sensitivity contested.

tracker.one_line: says which signals lead and which lag
tracker.premise_shape: In <domain>, <signal A> moves before <signal B> by <lag>, because <mechanism>.
tracker.falsifier: B moves first, or the stated lag fails
tracker.predict_frame: Report the current values of the leading and lagging signals and the observed gap. State what the lead predicts for the lagging signal, with a date.
tracker.assess_frame: Did the leading signal move first this period, and did the lag hold?

classifier.premise_shape: Cases with <feature> belong to <class 1>, not <class 2>, because <mechanism>.
classifier.falsifier: a case it sorted one way behaves like the other class
classifier.predict_frame: Sort the observed cases into the model's classes and state, for each, what behaviour would show the sorting was wrong.
classifier.assess_frame: Did any case sorted by this model behave like the other class?

adversary.one_line: attacks a common belief and names what would refute the attack
adversary.premise_shape: <Common belief> is wrong because <mechanism>. It would survive if <specific observation>.
adversary.falsifier: the belief under attack survives the specific test named
adversary.predict_frame: State the belief under attack and the specific observation that would vindicate it. An adversary that cannot be refuted by the thing it attacks is not doing its job.
adversary.assess_frame: Did the attacked belief survive the test this model named?

tracer.one_line: says how something travels -- which move causes which
tracer.premise_shape: In <domain>, <event A> moves <event B> before <event C>, via <mechanism>.
tracer.falsifier: the chain runs in a different order, or skips a named link
tracer.predict_frame: Trace the propagation path and state the ORDER in which the next links should fire.
tracer.assess_frame: Did the chain fire in the stated order?

timer.falsifier: the phase does not arrive in the stated window
timer.predict_frame: Name the phase, the window, and the observable that marks its arrival.
timer.assess_frame: Did the phase arrive inside the window?

attributor.premise_shape: <Outcome> was caused by <cause>, not <rival cause>, because <discriminator>.
attributor.falsifier: the outcome is better explained by a cause the model excluded
attributor.predict_frame: For each outcome, name the cause AND the leading rival cause, and the observation that discriminates between them.
attributor.assess_frame: Did the discriminating observation favour the named cause or the rival?

finder.premise_shape: Instances of <pattern> exist in <domain> and are findable by <method>.
finder.falsifier: it fails to surface an instance that later proves to have been findable
finder.predict_frame: Surface candidate instances and state what would show a missed one.
finder.assess_frame: Did an instance surface later that this model should have found?

generator.falsifier: OPEN. A generator that only produces plausible output is unfalsifiable. Candidate discipline: it must state what it will NOT generate, and be wrong when that appears.
generator.predict_frame: Generate candidates AND state the class of thing this model claims it will not produce. That negative claim is the only falsifiable part.
generator.assess_frame: Did something appear that this model said it would not generate?
generator.warning: This kind has no proven discipline. Building one is research, not scaffolding.

mirror.one_line: models the modeller -- one level up
mirror.falsifier: OPEN. Candidate discipline: it predicts a specific revision the author will make, and the author does not make it.
mirror.predict_frame: State a specific, dated revision you expect the author's own models to undergo.
mirror.warning: This kind has no proven discipline. Building one is research, not scaffolding.
